scope_note: Slice 4 (2026-08-19-slice-04-tenant-setup). Nine incidents selected for having a full symptom-to-regression narrative recoverable from the artifacts (an actual bug investigated with a stated hypothesis, a minimal check, and a verified root cause) — as opposed to the much larger set of Minor findings recorded in review-ledger.json, most of which are polish or scope calls rather than debugging narratives. DBG-DOH-02 and DBG-DOH-03 are two distinct findings from the same review round (review-49300d0..312ea96.diff) against the same file; DBG-DOH-05 and DBG-DOH-06 are the same module's dead-control defect across two rounds, the second being the first round's own fix reaching only part of the problem. Every field is cited to a report file, progress.md line range, or commit sha; no symptom, hypothesis, or root cause is stated here without a citing artifact.

entries.title: The fixed-path scratch-probe race (slice-03-gates.test.ts)
entries.symptom: tests/coverage/slice-03-gates.test.ts failed intermittently under concurrent pnpm test:release runs, 11-15 assertions at a time, with ENOENT and 'expected \'\' to contain …Probe.tsx'. Three separate agents lost time to it across the slice.
entries.expected: A clean 138/138 release-suite run regardless of what else is running concurrently in the same tree.
entries.actual: ENOENT reading app/super-admin/zz-probe/Probe.tsx and phantom timeouts, reproduced deliberately once before any fix: two pnpm test:release processes at once produced 8-10 failures with exactly this symptom.
entries.reproduction: Launch two `pnpm test:release` processes concurrently on the same working tree.
entries.evidence: infra-fixes-report.md:95-98 (deliberate baseline reproduction); progress.md:480-486 (three agents' worth of lost time recorded before the fix was dispatched).
entries.hypothesis: withPlanted() always wrote to one literal path (app/super-admin/zz-probe/Probe.tsx); two concurrent processes raced on that single path, one process's `finally` (rmSync) deleting the file mid-assertion in the other.
entries.minimal_check: Read withPlanted()'s implementation directly; confirmed the literal path is shared across all invocations rather than parameterized per process.
entries.root_cause: Cause A (fixed probe path) as hypothesized, PLUS two more causes found only after fixing A: Cause B — saSources()'s walk() recurses into every directory under SA_ROOT including a sibling process's differently-named probe directory once each process got its own path, so removing the shared-path race exposed a cross-process interference race underneath it; Cause C — tsconfig's **/*.tsx include glob makes any probe visible to a concurrent `pnpm typecheck`, found by the controller by accident mid-run (TS6053 naming a path that no longer existed).
entries.correction: Per-process, dot-prefixed probe directory (.zz-probe-<pid>); walk() and every other reader excludes foreign probe directories; mkdirSync/writeFileSync moved inside the try so a partial plant still hits cleanup; a module-level process.on('exit', ...) handler as a second, independent cleanup path.
entries.regression: Detection-preservation re-proved three separate times (original file, after pid-suffix+walk-exclusion, after dot-prefix+exit-handler) by dropping the 'i' flag from PERSON_DIMENSION and confirming the same three named assertions go red each time, reverting byte-identical each time.
entries.gate: tests/coverage/slice-03-gates.test.ts itself (the fixed gate); acceptance test was `pnpm test:release` x2 concurrent, 5 trials, 48/48 in every trial for this specific file.
entries.status: CLOSED at round 0 (commit 312ea96) — but its own fix under-covered call sites; see DBG-DOH-02.

entries.title: The round-0 race fix itself reached one reader of five (this slice's fourth instance of 'fix reaches one call site of several')
entries.symptom: Round-0's fix filtered walk() only. Independent review found four OTHER readdirSync(SA_ROOT) call sites in the same file still unfiltered, each stat'ing or reading every entry it listed.
entries.expected: Every reader of SA_ROOT excludes foreign probes, not only the one the original bug report happened to name.
entries.actual: declaredActions() (the widest window — runs outside any withPlanted, so it overlaps a sibling's plant naturally) plus three more sites were still exposed to the exact ENOENT symptom three agents had already lost time to. No logical false failure had yet been observed from these specific sites, but the requirement was judged incapable, not unlikely: 'five clean trials do not establish impossibility for a microsecond window.'
entries.reproduction: Independent review counted every readdirSync(SA_ROOT) occurrence in the file by inspection rather than by triggering a failure.
entries.hypothesis: A fix scoped to the one function named in the bug report, rather than to the shared root cause (every reader of SA_ROOT needs the same exclusion).
entries.minimal_check: grep/read every readdirSync(SA_ROOT) call site in tests/coverage/slice-03-gates.test.ts.
entries.root_cause: No single shared helper existed; each reader implemented its own directory listing, so a fix to one did not propagate to the others. Explicitly named as the fourth recurrence of this shape in the slice: a dead-control fix reaching one of three call sites (task 6), a state fold applied to one render branch of four (task 5), a pointer fix that created a new unpinned pointer (task 8), and this.
entries.correction: One shared isForeignProbe predicate and one saEntries() helper; every one of the five sites (plus walk() itself) now routes through it. readdirSync(SA_ROOT) appears exactly once in the file, inside saEntries().
entries.regression: Re-ran the same three-checkpoint detection-preservation proof a fourth time; identical three assertions red, revert byte-identical.
entries.gate: Independent review of the round-0 fix (review-49300d0..312ea96.diff), Important-1; closed in round 1, commit 9342ecd.

entries.title: Gate-evasion-by-naming: the probe-exclusion regex was a prefix match
entries.symptom: The exclusion regex /^\.?zz-probe/ matched anything merely starting with that prefix, at any depth, including real files — not only the scratch directories the fix was meant to hide from a race.
entries.expected: The exclusion matches only the exact scratch-directory names this code can itself create, and nothing else.
entries.actual: A real source file such as src/ui/sa/zz-probe.tsx or app/super-admin/<module>/zz-probeHelpers.tsx would have been silently invisible to every gate in the file — a real violation, hidden by the very fix meant to remove a false failure.
entries.reproduction: Planted a genuine violation file literally named zz-probe.tsx containing a forbidden-word string, ran the gate under the OLD prefix regex, confirmed it was NOT caught; ran it under the corrected exact regex, confirmed it WAS caught.
entries.evidence: infra-fixes-report.md:333-348 (Important 2, and its round-3 correction); progress.md:1101-1104, 1149-1152.
entries.hypothesis: A prefix match was chosen for convenience (probe dirs might vary slightly) without considering it also matches unrelated real files.
entries.minimal_check: Regex trace by hand: /^\.?zz-probe/.test('zz-probe.tsx') === true; the intended target is only .zz-probe-<pid>.
entries.root_cause: Same root as DBG-DOH-02's fix, applied without a matching-both-directions proof: the regex was verified to catch the intended target but never verified NOT to catch unintended ones.
entries.correction: Tightened to /^\.zz-probe-\d+$/ — matches only the exact directory name this code can ever create.
entries.regression: Re-verified in both directions (real file not hidden; real probe not missed) by the round-1 scoped re-review, independently of the implementer's own claim; process.pid is always a positive integer so every probe this code can construct matches unconditionally.
entries.gate: Same review chain as DBG-DOH-02, plus a distinct evidence-integrity finding recorded separately (see verification-ledger.json VER rows on the three-run sequence) because the implementer's first proof of this fix was judged reconstructable from source rather than run-specific.

entries.title: Two-cascade shared-state collision (MOD-DOH-02, Location Configuration)
entries.symptom: Round 1's own fix — keying the archival cascade scope per Job rather than per cascade node — made a previously 'unreachable' state reachable: a site-level archival with a held child cascade now SUCCEEDS instead of being wrongly refused, so one user action renders two simultaneous pending-cascade blocks. Both blocks' 'Reassign the paused Job to' selects were bound to a single shared useState.
entries.expected: Each cascade block's reassignment select is independent; choosing a destination in one must not affect the other, and acting on either must name that cascade's own Job and chosen Area.
entries.actual: Choosing a destination in one select silently showed the same choice in the other, and acting could name an Area the user never chose for that Job — on the one screen whose audit sentence is explicitly the product.
entries.reproduction: Component test drives the real UI: archives SITE-ARD-01 through the actual control and its STATE-04 confirmation dialog while the pre-seeded Paint Line cascade is held, producing two simultaneous cascade blocks by the same action a reviewer would take.
entries.hypothesis: A control whose target is not the one the screen names — the same defect class this module had already shipped once before, in its dead-control finding.
entries.minimal_check: Restore the shared 'shared' key (revert reassignTargetByNode to one fixed key) and re-run the module's component suite.
entries.root_cause: reassignTargetByNode was keyed on a single fixed string rather than on cascade.nodeId, so two concurrently-rendered selects wrote to and read from the same state slot.
entries.correction: Key the target per cascade node (reassignTargetByNode, a Record keyed on cascade.nodeId); each select reads/writes only its own key; the label carries the node so the two differ by accessible name too.
entries.regression: Mutation proof: reverting to the shared key reds exactly 'keys the reassignment destination per cascade, so two held archivals cannot share one target' (1 failed | 45 passed). Reverted and diffed against a pre-mutation copy (REVERT CLEAN).
entries.gate: Task 6 round-2 scoped re-review (review-727c49a..d86808b.diff) — verified all three read/write points (select value, onChange, reassignJob's resolve), not only the state's shape.

entries.title: The dead controls behind a green suite (MOD-DOH-02 initial build)
entries.symptom: The inherited Location Configuration screen typechecked and its suites were green, yet 'Create a Site' and 'Create an Area' visibly did nothing observable: the buttons wrote state that was then invisible forever.
entries.expected: A control that mutates state makes that mutation visible somewhere the same screen reads.
entries.actual: The scope filter closed over a fixture snapshot computed once at module load rather than the live state the buttons wrote to, so a newly created Site or Area could never appear in any filtered view. 'Green plus silent' — nothing about compiling or passing tests proved a control's effect ever reached the screen.
entries.reproduction: Press 'Create a Site' or 'Create an Area' in the running screen and observe the new entity never appears in any scope-filtered list.
entries.evidence: progress.md:258 ('Task 6: finisher DONE_WITH_CONCERNS...two of its controls did nothing'); commit 532c39e.
entries.hypothesis: A filter reads a cached/frozen snapshot of the fixture rather than the mutable state the write handlers update.
entries.minimal_check: Trace the scope-filter function's data source back to its definition — module-load constant vs. live useState.
entries.root_cause: AREA_BY_ID (and the analogous Site lookup) were built once from the frozen fixture at module load, never rebuilt from the live register the create-handlers wrote to.
entries.correction: Reproduced, root-caused, fixed, and pinned with regression tests that fail if the filter reverts to reading the module-load snapshot; 'Create a Location' (named by CTL-02 but never built at all) was also built in the same pass.
entries.regression: Five new regression tests, explicitly scrutinized by the controller's dispatch instruction as the thing to check hardest: 'a regression test that would still pass with the snapshot read restored is worth nothing.'
entries.gate: Task 6 initial independent review (review-392e47e..532c39e.diff) — found the fix reached only one of three call sites reading the same stale snapshot (see DBG-DOH-06).
entries.status: CLOSED (as a symptom) — its own fix was itself incomplete; continued as DBG-DOH-06.

entries.title: The dead-control fix reached one of three call sites (MOD-DOH-02 round-1 review finding)
entries.symptom: areaById still resolved from AREA_BY_ID, built once from the frozen fixture, at two of its call sites — both on WRITE paths.
entries.expected: Every consumer of the Area/Site lookup reads the live register, not a mix of live and frozen.
entries.actual: One call site left a third enabled control that did nothing on a reachable path (create an Area, select it as a re-parent target, press the enabled button, nothing happens, forever); the other fell back to reparentTargets[0], so choosing a newly created Area silently reassigned the Job to a DIFFERENT Area — and the audit sentence named that other Area, on the screen whose audit sentence is the product.
entries.reproduction: Independent review traced both write-path call sites of areaById/siteById directly, without needing to trigger the UI.
entries.evidence: progress.md:296-304 (Important-1 of the task-6 round-1 review).
entries.hypothesis: Same as DBG-DOH-05's root cause, unaddressed at two of its three call sites — the fix patched the branch the original finding named and left two more behind it.
entries.minimal_check: grep for every remaining areaById/siteById/AREA_BY_ID/SITE_BY_ID occurrence in the screen.
entries.root_cause: The initial fix (commit 532c39e) closed the read path the finding demonstrated but did not sweep the file for every other reader of the same stale snapshot.
entries.correction: The screen no longer imports areaById or siteById at all; one liveArea/liveSite pair resolves from live state, the root the prior fix only reached a branch of.
entries.regression: Task 6 round-1 re-review counted the sweep itself: grep for every prior stale-read symbol returns zero occurrences; the four remaining module-load reads were individually judged non-stale (useState seeds, a per-role scope declaration no control edits, visible-id sets on personas that cannot create, and two frozen vocabularies).
entries.status: CLOSED — but its own fix created the reachable two-cascade collision, DBG-DOH-04.

entries.title: The STATE-01 fold applied to one render branch of four (MOD-DOH-12, SSO connection)
entries.symptom: Selecting STATE-01 as Tenant Admin produced a card reading 'Configured — a connection record exists and the email domains below resolve onto it' two paragraphs above 'No protocol is in force and no domain resolves onto this record' on the same screen.
entries.expected: A screen showing one connection state must not simultaneously assert and deny that a connection record is in force.
entries.actual: The `configured` fold only wrapped `stateId === 'STATE-01'` into the ternary controlling the status pill's origin data; the status pill and the state-meaning text rendered straight off connection.state OUTSIDE that ternary — two more paths off the same unfolded root: the test-connection check printed a resolution 'against the record above' while the card said no record was in force, and the metadata-save announcement said the record 'reads as configured' while the card kept rendering the empty shape.
entries.reproduction: Select STATE-01 as the Tenant Admin persona and read the two contradictory sentences on one screen.
entries.hypothesis: A derived-value fold applied at one render call site does not propagate to sibling call sites reading the same underlying field directly.
entries.minimal_check: grep every render/resolve statement in the screen for raw reads of the `connection` identifier vs. reads of the folded value.
entries.root_cause: Four render/resolve paths off one root (`connection.state`) each needed to agree, and 'four branches each remembering to check cannot be relied on' — precisely the shape of the defect.
entries.correction: One derived `connectionShown` feeds all fourteen (re-counted as fifteen) render and resolve reads; writes deliberately keep reading the raw record (a separate, commented exception) because persisting the coercion would store a state the record does not have.
entries.regression: Task 5 round-1 re-review counted the reads itself: sixteen property accesses across fifteen distinct statements (not the report's claimed fourteen), then ran an independent word-boundary grep confirming no raw `connection` read remains on any render path.
entries.gate: Task 5 initial review (review-5288b55..0766c90.diff) then round-1 re-review (review-ffffd3f..ed2d0f7.diff).

entries.title: Scope enforced in what the screen drew, not in what it read (MOD-DOH-04, Worker Lifecycle and Qualifications)
entries.symptom: The clearance corpus rendered on screen was unfiltered for every persona while the module's own matrix row, printed on the same screen, stated the view was scope-filtered for the Supervisor.
entries.expected: A screen that states an enforcement on its own matrix must actually perform that enforcement on every read and write path it controls.
entries.actual: A Supervisor scoped to Paint and Assembly could read two Polish-area clearances and their free-text reasons; separately, the qualification-write checkboxes were bounded only by which Areas rendered for the current persona, so the selected ids survived a persona switch — a Tenant Admin could tick Quality Laboratory, switch to Supervisor, and write a qualification scoped to an Area Supervisor does not hold.
entries.reproduction: Independent review compared row sets between personas directly (the sweep that WOULD catch this loops one persona at a time and never compares row sets between them — which is why no test had caught it).
entries.evidence: progress.md:1131-1139 (task-9 independent review, both Important findings, described as 'one blind spot').
entries.hypothesis: A value legitimately scoped for DISPLAY (checkbox availability, Select options) was trusted as if it also BOUNDED what got read into a corpus or written into a record, while the underlying register stayed unscoped.
entries.minimal_check: The file already solved the identical hazard one line away, for the Area FILTER, with the reasoning written in a comment: 'A filter naming an Area this persona cannot see is not a filter, so it falls back rather than being reset in whichever handler we remembered.'
entries.root_cause: Render-time bounding (which controls are drawn) was conflated with data-time bounding (which records are read into a corpus or accepted on write) in two of the module's paths, while a third path (the Area filter) already had the correct fix.
entries.correction: Both fixes applied by intersection with the persona's live Area scope, following the file's own existing pattern rather than inventing a new one; a second leak site (the clearance history read) was found and fixed by the implementer beyond what the review named.
entries.regression: Subset proof checked in both directions (removing the filter reds the case; a filter returning an empty array also reds it — equality is not a pass and neither is emptiness). Re-review confirmed the intersection shape structurally: changeScenario touches neither value, both are recomputed every render from the live role.
entries.gate: Task 9 initial review (review-312ea96..2dcd236.diff) then round-1 re-review (review-9342ecd..f20e68e.diff). The generalisation ('anything bounding a write by render has the same defect class') was judged sound and mechanisable, carried toward a task-11 gate.
entries.status: CLOSED — generalisation not yet enforced as a gate (task 11 not reached in this workspace).

entries.title: workerById reading a module-load Map instead of the live register (MOD-DOH-04) — the third instance of the module-load-snapshot defect in this slice
entries.symptom: A seed-built lookup (`new Map(...)`) existed for resolving a worker by id, alongside the module's other lookups which already took the live register.
entries.expected: Every lookup that can be affected by a write in this session reads the live register, with no module-load-frozen alternative left in the file.
entries.actual: workerById's signature took the frozen module-load Map. At the time it was found it had zero production call sites — it existed only for the calendar module (task 10) that had not yet been built.
entries.reproduction: grep -n "new Map(" fixtures.ts, before and after the fix.
entries.evidence: progress.md:1141, 1193, 1256-1258 (task-9 independent review Minor promoted to a fix, and the round-1 re-review's explicit instruction to COUNT every seed-built lookup rather than confirm only the one named).
entries.hypothesis: Same class as DBG-DOH-05/06 (module-load snapshot vs. live state) and named explicitly as this slice's third occurrence of it.
entries.minimal_check: Count every seed-built (`new Map(`, similar) lookup in the module, not only the one the review named.
entries.root_cause: An interface authored against the seed data at the time no live-register-consuming call site existed yet, left unrevised once a sibling call site (workerById's own module) did switch to the live register.
entries.correction: workerById's signature changed to take the live register directly; the module-load Map deleted.
entries.regression: Re-review counted the seed-built lookups itself as instructed: one existed, it is gone, and every other lookup in the module already took its register — grep confirms zero remaining `new Map(` calls.
entries.status: CLOSED — closed before any consumer (task 10's calendar) existed, which the build's own commit message calls 'the cheapest moment an interface can be corrected.'
entries.source_citation: progress.md:1141, 1193, 1256-1258; commit f20e68e; commit 75732ea ('task 10a...consumes all three [interface fixes]')
